description: Maps raw scanner keys (from the syn visitor in src/analyze.rs) to lust feature status. The orchestrator updates status and milestone as lust grows. A later `lust capabilities --json` can feed this file: use --capabilities <file> with the same {features:[{id,status,milestone}]} shape to override entries by id. Patterns are globs: * matches any text, all other characters are literal. First matching feature in file order wins for a raw key, so specific rules come before general ones. primary_keys select which raw keys create a finding; keys select which raw keys block a file in the coverage curve. Statuses are measured, not hand-kept: scripts/port-scan-sync.py runs the probes in tools/lust-port/tests/features/ against rustc and writes status plus milestone (notes stay hand-written). Run it after each wave, then run it again with --coverage.

milestones.label: The Rust core (modules, cfg, const/static, tuples, arrays, slices, Box, Result, Drop, std basics, macro_rules!)
Traits, closures, dyn, Rc (generics, iterators, Rc/RefCell, dyn Trait, built-in dependency layer)
Lifetimes ('static and '_ first, then lifetime params on user types)
Threads and panics (sync, atomics, mpsc, panic recovery, C shims)
Port ts-rust (checked rewrites, small async state machine for ATA)

features.title: Supported baseline (elided refs, core derives, doc/test attrs)
features.notes: Keys here are accepted by lust today and never block a file.

features.title: User macro_rules! definitions and calls
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/macros_user.rs and macros_user_b.rs pass against rustc 1.99 (expr, ident, ty and recursive tt macros).

features.title: #[path] module attribute
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/modules_path_attr.rs passes (sibling file through #[path]).

features.title: async fn, async blocks and .await
features.notes: No general async executor is planned. Milestone 8b allows a small state machine for ATA in ts-rust.

features.title: impl Trait in argument position
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/traits_impl_trait_arg.rs, _b, _c, and _d pass (fx-impl-arg): impl Display, Iterator adapters and consumers on an impl Iterator arg, impl Into<String> from &str/String/&String/char (std From impls for String, Box, Rc, and From<T> for T), and impl Trait inside an item binding (impl IntoIterator<Item = impl Into<String>>). Gaps (rejects): a user Iterator type passed to an impl Iterator arg that runs adapters (needs the unfused path), ExactSizeIterator<Item = ..> bindings, Into::into as a fn value, Rc<T> from Box<T>, Into<Arc<str>>.

features.title: Const generic parameters and const type arguments
features.notes: Not a compiler milestone in PLAN.md. Milestone 8 closes it by a checked rewrite: specialize the few functions by hand (3 in ts-rust).

features.title: Explicit for<'a> higher-ranked binders
features.notes: Rank-one binders are part of milestone 6. Rare explicit cases can often drop the binder.

features.title: Implicit higher-ranked Fn(&T) bounds
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/closures_hrtb_bounds.rs passes (Fn(&T) and FnMut(&str) bounds). Explicit for<'a> stays in lifetimes.hrtb.

features.title: Send and Sync bounds
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/threads_send_sync_bounds.rs and _b pass. Send and Sync are accepted as marker bounds, also on dyn. Real threads stay in threads.sync.

features.title: impl Drop
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/core_drop_impl.rs passes, drop runs at scope end in rustc order.

features.title: 'static and '_ lifetimes, std lifetime carriers
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/lifetimes_static_anon.rs, _b and _c pass: &'static refs and fields, T: 'static, Formatter<'_> in Display impls, and a named std carrier in a return type (slice Iter<'_>).

features.title: Named lifetimes, lifetime params on user types, reference fields
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/lifetimes_named.rs, _b and _c pass: lifetime params on structs and enums, ref fields, named fn lifetimes, outlives, and &'a self receivers. Fn-pointer lifetime types are split into closures.fn_ptr_lifetime.

features.title: LazyLock and OnceLock statics
features.notes: Part of the milestone 5 std runtime, not threads.

features.title: Panic recovery (catch_unwind, resume_unwind, panic hooks)
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/panic_recovery*.rs pass under panic=unwind (W-UNWIND): catch_unwind with AssertUnwindSafe, set_hook/take_hook, resume_unwind, thread join Err and Mutex poisoning. A Cargo package unwinds by its dev profile; a single file needs -C panic=unwind. Gaps: thread::Builder (L0505), a hook closure that calls a captured Box<dyn Fn> (L0820).

features.title: thread_local! statics
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/threads_thread_local.rs fails with the unsafe reject inside the macro form (L0404). Split from threads.sync: ts-rust keeps per-thread caches in program.rs and the scanner.

features.title: unsafe blocks and unsafe fns
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/unsafe_blocks.rs fails (L0404). PLAN.md keeps unsafe opt-in for C shims. Split from cinterop.system so plain unsafe use does not count as a system crate.

features.title: Threads and synchronization (Arc, Mutex, atomics, mpsc)
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/threads_sync.rs and _b fail at the Arc and atomic type names (L0101, L0102). thread_local! is split into threads.thread_local. Real threads are required; a one-thread rewrite slows the shipped binary.

features.title: Raw pointer types as identity values (*const T, *mut T)
features.notes: Split from cinterop.system (w-cinterop). Probe: cinterop_raw_ptr.rs: coercion from references, core::ptr::from_ref/null/eq, cast, addr, Eq/Ord/Hash by address, Rc::as_ptr. No deref: that needs unsafe (unsafe.blocks) and stays rejected.

features.title: extern blocks and extern fn ABI
features.notes: Split from cinterop.system (w-cinterop). Probe: cinterop_extern.rs (the old cinterop_system.rs): a foreign fn call needs unsafe (unsafe.blocks) plus the extern surface; lust rejects both today (L0810, L0404).

features.title: #[global_allocator] statics
features.notes: Split from cinterop.system (w-cinterop). Probe: cinterop_global_allocator.rs with std::alloc::System. ts-rust's bins name tikv_jemallocator::Jemalloc, which also needs that adapter crate.

features.title: System crates (rustix, nix, signal-hook, jemalloc, zlib, local time)
features.notes: Cached rustc-built C ABI shims in milestone 7. See dependencies.json for the per-crate decision. Split by w-cinterop: raw pointer types are cinterop.raw_ptr, extern blocks are cinterop.extern, and #[global_allocator] is cinterop.global_allocator. No probe: each crate needs its own adapter probe.

features.title: Attributes and cfg lust accepts (cfg, cfg_attr, inline, cold, repr, must_use, allow, default, rustfmt, ignore, should_panic)
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/attrs_cfg.rs, _b, _c and _d pass: cfg, cfg!, cfg_attr, inline, cold, must_use, allow, repr, path, the derive(Default) helper #[default] on a unit variant, the inert tool attributes rustfmt::* and clippy::*, and the test harness attributes ignore and should_panic in a normal build (lust test honors them; see tests/testrun). Serde helper attributes are split into attrs.serde. Attribute names lust rejects are split into attrs.unsupported.

features.title: #[track_caller] on user fns and std::panic::Location
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/attrs_track_caller.rs (W-CHECK-G3): a hidden caller-location parameter; panics and Location::caller() in the fn report the caller's location. Gaps (rejects): on trait methods, and the fn as a value (fn pointer, dyn Fn, generic F: Fn argument).

features.title: #[non_exhaustive] on structs, enums, and variants
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/attrs_non_exhaustive.rs passes (fx-attrs): collect records the mark on the Adt and each variant; across a crate border, struct literals and tuple or unit constructors of a marked type are private, named-field patterns need .., and a match needs a wildcard. Inside the defining crate nothing changes.

features.title: #[serde(...)] helper attributes of the serde derives
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/attrs_serde.rs is a lust-only oracle and lust rejects it (L0402). The attribute only has meaning under derive(Serialize) or derive(Deserialize), which lust also rejects (derives.unknown), so accepting and ignoring it would change program behavior. It stays a clean reject.

features.title: Attribute names lust rejects
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/attrs_unsupported.rs fails (L0402). The attr.* catch-all lives here, after the accepted names in attrs.cfg and the serde names in attrs.serde, so a new attribute name blocks a file until lust knows it.

features.title: dyn Any and downcast
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/dyn_any.rs and _b pass (W-CHECK-G3): Any, TypeId, type_id, is, downcast_ref, downcast_mut, Box and Rc downcast, Any as a supertrait, Debug for dyn Any. Gaps (rejects): Debug, Hash, and Ord of TypeId (rustc prints and orders its hash values); a non-turbofish reference type as an Any type; a user blanket impl whose where clause excludes a dyn receiver is still taken by the method probe (L0612).

features.title: dyn Fn, FnMut and FnOnce objects
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/dyn_fn.rs, _b and _c pass: &dyn Fn, &mut dyn FnMut and Rc<dyn Fn> fields, the callback shape in ts-rust program.rs. Arc<dyn Fn> waits for Arc (std.sync).

features.title: dyn over std traits (io::Write, fmt, Future)
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/dyn_std.rs fails (L0102): &mut dyn io::Write. Lust dyn covers crate traits (dyn.trait); std trait objects need their own vtables. dyn Fn, Any, and Send and Sync claims come earlier in this table.

features.title: &dyn and &mut dyn Trait over crate traits
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/dyn_trait.rs passes: &dyn and &mut dyn over crate traits. Owned dyn, dyn Fn, dyn over std traits and impl Trait returns are split into dyn.boxed, dyn.fn, dyn.std and traits.impl_trait_ret.

features.title: Owned dyn values (Box<dyn>, Rc<dyn>, Arc<dyn>)
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/dyn_boxed.rs passes: Box<dyn Tr> and Rc<dyn Tr> (drop through the vtable, upcasts, Rc counts). Arc<dyn Tr> waits for Arc. dyn_in.& and dyn_in.&mut stay in dyn.trait, which comes first; every other dyn_in wrapper lands here.

features.title: impl Trait in return position
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/traits_impl_trait_ret.rs passes (W-CHECK-G3): callers check in an opaque view (bounds, auto-trait leakage) and a revealed check that replays its picks. Iterator adapters and consumers on an impl Iterator value work (fx-impl-arg). Gaps (rejects): impl Trait in traits; generic callers (template borrowck, L0602); a hidden type that is Copy where the bounds are not (L0602). Argument position is traits.impl_trait_arg.

features.title: Rc (plain, sized)
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/std_rc.rs passes: Rc::new, clone and strong_count on a sized type. Weak and the cell types stay in std.rc_refcell, Rc<dyn> in dyn.boxed.

features.title: Weak, RefCell, Cell and OnceCell
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/std_rc_refcell_b.rs, _c and _d fail: Weak is an unknown type (L0102), RefCell and Cell are not implemented (L0641), OnceCell is unknown (L0102). Plain Rc is split into std.rc; Cow is split into std.cow.

features.title: Cow (borrowed or owned strings and slices)
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/std_cow.rs fails (L0102): Cow<'_, str> returns, as in ts-rust normalize_slashes_cow. Split from std.rc_refcell, which held every std::borrow path.

features.title: Wider std runtime (collections, time, hash, ptr, fmt traits, pin, ffi, os)
features.notes: Milestone 5. Some paths here only need trait support from the same milestone.

features.title: Fn pointer types with lifetimes
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/closures_fn_ptr_lifetime.rs fails (L0203): fn(&'a str) -> &'a str stored in a struct field, as in ts-rust ast/synthetic. The scanner emits type.fn_ptr.lifetime for this form; plain fn pointers pass under closures.general.

features.title: General closures, fn pointers and fn-valued fields
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/closures_general.rs passes: closures to user fns, move captures, fn pointer values. Dyn Fn forms are split into dyn.fn and dyn.boxed.

features.title: Iterator chains, adapters, collect and for over method calls
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/iterators_chains.rs and _b pass: map, filter, collect, sum, skip, take, for over arrays, Vec, &Vec, ranges and chars.

features.title: Generic associated types
features.notes: GATs are explicitly out of PLAN.md (What we will not do).

features.title: User traits, trait impls, generics, bounds and associated types
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/traits_generics.rs, _b and _c pass: user traits, default and associated items, where clauses, operator impls and a blanket impl.

features.title: Modules, glob imports and re-exports
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/modules_imports.rs and _b pass: inline and file mods, globs, re-exports, renames and trait imports as _.

features.title: const, static, const fn, type aliases, tuple structs, explicit discriminants, nested fns
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/core_items.rs passes: const, static, const fn, aliases, tuple structs, explicit discriminants and nested fns.

features.title: Tuples, arrays, slices and range indexing
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/core_tuples_arrays_slices.rs passes, including inferred and never types in annotations.

features.title: Labels, struct update, if-let chains, let-else, reference/tuple/slice patterns, const blocks
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/core_patterns_control.rs, _b and _c pass: let-else, let chains, labels, struct update, slice, tuple, struct, or, range, nested and ref patterns, and let without init.

features.title: Result, ? operator and Box
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/core_result_try.rs and _b pass: ? with a From conversion, Result matching, Box deref and recursive Box fields.

features.title: HashMap and HashSet with an explicit hasher type
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/std_hashmap_hasher.rs passes (W-STD-B). The scanner emits map.hasher_arg when a collections map has a third type arg, the shape behind FxHashMap aliases and ts-rust CacheKeyHasher maps.

features.title: HashMap and HashSet
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/std_hashmap.rs passes (W-STD-B). Split from core.std_basics so mem and cmp files do not count as blocked by maps they never use.

features.title: Std basics: mem, env, process, fs, io, path, str, cmp, char, num, slice, HashMap/HashSet
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/core_std_basics.rs passes: mem::take and swap, cmp helpers, str methods. _b, _c and _d fail: std::fs::metadata path form (L0505), the Path type and io::Write into a Vec (L0101), and primitive From paths such as i64::from (L0101). HashMap is split into std.hashmap.

features.title: u128/i128, f32/f64, float literals and extended format specs
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/core_numbers_format.rs and _b pass: u128, f32 and f64, width, precision and radix specs, radix, byte, char, raw-string and suffix literals.

features.title: Derives Default, PartialOrd and Ord
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/core_derives_extra.rs passes: Default, PartialOrd and Ord derives drive comparisons and default values.

features.title: Std macros lust does not expand yet (write!, writeln!, include_bytes!)
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/macros_std_unsupported.rs passes (write! and writeln! into a String under `use std::fmt::Write as _;`). _b passes (W-CHECK-G3): include_bytes! is a byte string literal of the exact bytes, &[u8; N], binary data included. Gap: a blob past about 1 MB in a static, or a const fn loop past 1M steps over one, hits the const evaluator step cap (L0630, a reject). Split from macros.std_missing by macro name.

features.title: Std macros by name that lust expands (matches!, debug_assert!, include_str!, env!, concat!)
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/macros_std_missing.rs and _c pass: matches!, debug_assert!, vec! repeat, concat!, stringify!, env!, include_str!, line! and file!. The write! family and include_bytes! are split into macros.std_unsupported. Names not probed (option_env!, include!, compile_error!, module_path!, column!) follow the lust capabilities macro list.

features.title: Other constructs with no plan milestone (unions, trait aliases, negative/unsafe/auto traits, variadic, try blocks, box patterns)
features.notes: Not in PLAN.md. Needs a human decision per site.

features.title: Derives other than the lust set
features.notes: May be proc-macro derives from other crates. Proc macros stay out of PLAN.md.

features.title: Supported std core paths (Vec, String, Option)
features.notes: Common methods on these types work today. Method-level gaps that need closures or iterators are counted under those features.

features.title: External crate with no adapter decision yet
features.notes: Add a decision in dependencies.json and a rule here. Only crates in the scanner EXT list produce ext.* keys; other crates show in the dependency report as unknown.

features.title: TCP and UDP sockets (TcpStream, TcpListener, UdpSocket, Shutdown)
features.notes: Split from std.other (W-STD-C phase 2 scan). Owner: W-SHIM-P2 (system io, with io/fs/process). Probe: std_net.rs (loopback listener). The address types are std.net_addr.

features.title: IP and socket address types (IpAddr, SocketAddr, parsing)
features.notes: Split from std.other (W-STD-C phase 2). Probe: std_net_addr.rs. In lust std source (library/std/src/net.rs). str::parse is a str method and counts under its own state.

features.title: std::error::Error trait
features.notes: Split from std.other (W-STD-C phase 2); ts-rust has `use std::error::Error` with plain impls (impl.trait keys stay traits.generics). Probe: std_error.rs (impl through a bound). In lust std source (library/core/src/error.rs). dyn Error and source() chains stay with dyn.std (fmt supertraits in vtables, L0702).

features.title: std::f64::consts and std::f32::consts by full path
features.notes: Split from std.other (W-STD-C phase 2); the const evaluator has these since W-STD-C, only the row was missing. Probe: std_float_consts.rs (bits of PI, E, TAU, SQRT_2, FRAC_1_PI, LN_2).

features.title: std::vec::IntoIter named as a type
features.notes: Split from std.other (W-STD-C phase 2): supported.std_core claims the expr paths but only the exact Vec type. Probe: std_vec_into_iter.rs. Drain and Splice types stay with fx-vec-drain.

features.title: Other std paths not listed above
features.notes: Catch-all so a new std path blocks the file until it gets a precise rule. Add a precise entry when one appears.
